slot.brief: A wire stretched by known amount with a hanging mass; use Y = stress/strain to find elongation or the maximum load for a given breaking stress.

stem: A wire of length $1.5$ m and cross-sectional area $0.8$ mm$^2$ elongates by $0.3$ mm under a hanging mass of $4$ kg. If its breaking stress is $1.5 \times 10^8$ Pa, find its elongation at the breaking point. Take $g = 10$ m s$^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: At 4 kg, the stress is $40/(0.8\times10^{-6})=5\times10^7$ Pa. In the elastic range, elongation is proportional to stress, so at $1.5\times10^8$ Pa it is $0.3\times3=0.9$ mm.

working:
$A=0.8\times10^{-6}\ \text{m}^2$, $F=4\times10=40\ \text{N}$
$$Y=\frac{FL}{A\Delta L}=\frac{40\times1.5}{(0.8\times10^{-6})(0.3\times10^{-3})}=2.5\times10^{11}\ \text{Pa}$$
$$\Delta L_{\mathrm{break}}=L\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{break}}}{Y}=1.5\times\frac{1.5\times10^8}{2.5\times10^{11}}=0.9\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}=0.9\ \text{mm}$$

Independent check: At 4 kg, the stress is $40/(0.8\times10^{-6})=5\times10^7$ Pa. In the elastic range, elongation is proportional to stress, so at $1.5\times10^8$ Pa it is $0.3\times3=0.9$ mm.
